NavDescription: I am a current MSW student originally from East New York, Brooklyn, with a Bachelor of Technology in Canine Training & Management. As a queer woman, I strive to build open, comfortable, and inclusive spaces for everyone. I personally trained and certified my cat as a therapy animal, bringing comfort to local libraries, nursing homes, and healthcare facilities through animal-assisted activities.

NavDescription:
Amaya is a recent UAlbany alum who served as a hotline assistant with the Middle Earth Peer Assistance Program and supported first-year students' transitions into college through First-Year Experience programming and Writing and Critical Inquiry courses. 
Amaya is currently a Prevention Navigator for Project ACCESS, a prevention service grant aimed at helping minoritized students navigate health and well-being resources on-and off-campus. 
Amaya's academic interests center on trauma informed care and peer-to-peer support.  
In her free time, Amaya enjoys reading, watching movies, and spending time outside. 
Pronouns: she/her/hers, they/them/theirs

NavDescription: Amanda Fowler is a recent graduate of Binghamton University’s Master of Social Work Program. She earned her bachelor’s degree in human development & psychology with a minor in Sociology from University at Albany - SUNY. Amanda is passionate about advocating for and implementing harm reduction resources and strategies on college campuses. She is currently Project Manager for Project ACCESS. In her free time, she loves to play video games, watch football, workout, and spend time with loved ones. Pronouns: she/her/hers
